title: Foreign Trump Organization deals timed with tariff negotiations
summary: The list of foreign Trump-branded projects outside the Gulf is real: Vietnam, Indonesia, India, Serbia, Georgia, the Maldives and Romania, with CREW counting 21-25 foreign projects. Vietnam is the strong case: Hanoi fast-tracked the $1.5B Hung Yen project, reportedly bypassing its own legal steps, while negotiating down a threatened 46% tariff to 20%. Elsewhere the 'deals timed with tariff favours' framing does not hold up. Indonesia halted the MNC Lido project in Feb 2025. India's tariffs rose to 50% while Trump towers kept launching. No direct quid pro quo is documented anywhere. Every counterparty is a private developer, so the 2025 ethics policy permits the deals, though in several cases state approvals or state-linked land sit behind them. Audit update: per-project fees are partly documented: a $5M Vietnam licence fee from KBC's Hung Yen vehicle and at least $12M from India in 2024 (including a $10M Reliance development fee) appear in Trump's 2025 disclosure.

sub_claims.statement: CREW counts roughly two dozen foreign Trump-branded projects during the second term.
sub_claims.finding: CREW's foreign development tracker has been retitled as it grew: 21, then 24, then 25 projects 'developed in foreign countries during Trump's presidency'. The current page was not fetchable here (host blocked), so the latest count rests on search snippets. CREW says 13 were first announced after Trump became a candidate in 2022. CREW's analysis of the 2026 disclosure (covering 2025) puts foreign revenue above $117M in 2025, against at least $149M over the whole first term, with 28 foreign-project accounts reporting at least $50,000 (nine in 2020). The FT, as summarised in search results, puts foreign licensing, development and management revenue at $63M in 2025, up 40%. The totals depend on which categories are counted; CREW's figure includes foreign golf/hotel operating revenue, not just new licence fees.

sub_claims.statement: Vietnam: the $1.5B Hung Yen golf/urban project was fast-tracked while Vietnam negotiated tariffs.
sub_claims.finding: The deal with Kinh Bac City Development (KBC, a private Hanoi-listed industrial-park developer chaired by Dang Thanh Tam) was announced in October 2024, before the election. Its local vehicle is Hung Yen Hospitality Services. After Trump's 2 April 2025 threat of a 46% tariff on Vietnam, Deputy PM Tran Hong Ha signed in-principle investment approval in mid-May 2025 for the ~990-hectare, ~$1.5B Khoai Chau project. Eric Trump and PM Pham Minh Chinh broke ground on 21 May 2025. Chinh said Eric Trump's visit 'motivated us to expedite this project' and promised 'maximum support'. The New York Times (25 May 2025, via syndication and summaries; the original was not fetched) reported that legal experts said Vietnam skipped at least half a dozen legally required steps. It also published an official letter saying the project was receiving 'special attention from the Trump administration and President Donald Trump personally'. Reuters (Aug 2025) described Vietnam as having 'fast-tracked approvals as it negotiated a crucial trade deal with Washington'. The state pays farmer compensation of about $12-30/m2, though developers fund it; the Trump Organization says it is not involved in investment or compensation. Eviction notices were issued by June 2026, and the first phase is targeted for late 2027, around APEC in Vietnam.

Trump announced on 2 July 2025 that Vietnamese goods would pay 20% and transshipments 40%, down from the 46% threatened in April. A framework 'Agreement on Reciprocal, Fair, and Balanced Trade' joint statement followed on 26 Oct 2025 at the ASEAN summit, keeping 20% with some goods possibly going to zero. Vietnam did get substantial relief from the threatened rate. But 20% is still among the higher rates in the region, the deal was not finalised as of June 2026, and the US later opened trade-practice investigations into Vietnam. No source shows the golf project was part of the negotiation, and the White House says trade talks are 'totally unrelated to the Trump Organization'. The link is temporal and circumstantial.

sub_claims.statement: Vietnam: a Ho Chi Minh City Trump Tower.
sub_claims.finding: A Vietnamese government document reported by Reuters on 19 May 2025 showed the Trump Organization exploring a tower of at least 60 storeys and ~$1B in Thu Thiem, promoted by KBC and Saigon Invest Group, with in-principle government approval of the 'Trump Vietnam' programme. Reuters' source said work could start in 2026. I found no confirmed site approval, licence or groundbreaking as of Nov 2026, so the tower remains a proposal. CREW separately reported five new Trump trademark applications in Vietnam filed months after the lower tariff rate was agreed.

sub_claims.statement: Indonesia: MNC/Hary Tanoesoedibjo Trump resorts advanced while Indonesia negotiated tariffs.
sub_claims.finding: The Lido (West Java) and Bali (Tanah Lot) Trump projects with MNC Group/MNC Land, controlled by Hary Tanoesoedibjo, date from 2015-2019 and are not new second-term deals. Far from being fast-tracked, Indonesia's Environment Ministry ordered MNC Land on 6 Feb 2025 to halt development at Lido over water management and environmental violations. MNC Land denied fault and in March 2025 still announced the Trump-linked golf club. A single trade outlet (Golf Industry Asia, Aug 2026) reports the suspension was lifted after compliance, with the Trump golf course operating; that is uncorroborated. On the tariff side, the 32% threat was cut to 19% in a July 2025 deal, finalised in February 2026. The documented link is the 13 Oct 2025 Sharm el-Sheikh hot-mic exchange: Prabowo asked Trump to arrange a meeting with Eric and mentioned 'Hary', and Trump said he would have Eric call. Eric Trump later said he had not met Prabowo. That shows a foreign leader seeking to engage the family business, but no deal or tariff concession tied to it was found.

India is the largest foreign market for the brand. Business Today (Aug 2026) describes Trump Towers Hyderabad (Kokapet, two 65-storey towers, Tribeca Developers with Ira Realty) as the eighth Trump-branded project in India. Others include Trump World Center Pune, a commercial project with Kundan Spaces announced March 2025. Tribeca plans more in Gurgaon, Mumbai and elsewhere. The counterparties are private Indian developers led by Tribeca's Kalpesh Mehta, who attended the 2025 inauguration; none is state-linked. The tariff story cuts against a 'favour' narrative. The US raised India's tariff to 50% in August 2025 (25% reciprocal plus a 25% Russian-oil penalty) while Indian Trump launches continued, then cut it to 18% in February 2026 after India agreed to curb Russian oil purchases. I found no evidence connecting the licences to those decisions. Per-project India fees were not checked against the disclosure (search budget exhausted).

Already covered in C45. Kushner's Affinity Partners planned a ~$500M Trump-branded hotel/residential project on the former Yugoslav General Staff site under a 2024 deal with a 99-year rent-free lease. Parliament passed a special law on 7 Nov 2025 stripping the site's heritage status. The project collapsed on 15-16 Dec 2025 when prosecutors charged officials with forging the delisting documents and Affinity withdrew. This is a state counterparty (the Serbian government), but the Trump Organization's role was licensing via Kushner's fund. No tariff linkage was established here.

The project was reported by the WSJ and unveiled in April 2026: a ~70-storey mixed-use tower with Georgian developers (Archi Group, Biograpi Living, Blox Group, Finvest Georgia) and the US Sapir Organization, with a branding agreement reportedly signed in May 2026. Per the Guardian (May 2026) and WSJ (13 Sep 2026), as relayed by JAMnews and inkl, the land, a former racecourse, was bought by developers in 2023 for up to $85M from the Cartu fund linked to the family of Bidzina Ivanishvili. The US Treasury sanctioned Ivanishvili in December 2024. Georgian Dream officials presented the deal as a sign that relations 'have been restored', while the US had suspended its strategic partnership in November 2024 and the House passed the MEGOBARI sanctions bill. This is a favour-seeking pattern by a foreign ruling party rather than a tariff deal, and I found no US policy concession to Georgia tied to it. The White House says neither the president nor his family engages in conflicts of interest, and Ivanishvili's lawyer says most of the racecourse land was donated to the state for a park. The WSJ was not accessed directly.

Trump International Hotel Maldives was announced on 17 Nov 2025 with Dar Global (the private Saudi developer covered in C31): about 80 villas near Male, opening around end-2028. It is billed as the world's first tokenised hotel development, and Reuters (via The Block) reports Dar Global planned to fund up to 70% of the ~$300M project by selling tokens to US retail investors and was talking to the SEC. Neither a Maldivian state counterparty nor any Maldives-US policy outcome was found.

Trump Tower Bucharest was announced in July 2025 with SDC Imobiliare, a private Cluj developer, and a larger Cluj-Napoca golf/hotel project (>$500M per a Bloomberg-derived abstract) was planned for 2026. The Real Deal (March 2026) described the Bucharest site as stalled, with the rendering about double the zoning height limit, and a launch was delayed in December 2025. I found no state counterparty and no Romania-specific US concession.

sub_claims.statement: Fees paid to the Trump Organization for these foreign projects.
sub_claims.finding: Some per-project fees outside the Gulf are now documented from Trump's disclosures, though most remain undisclosed. Vietnam: Trump's June 2025 OGE report lists a $5M licence fee from Hung Yen Hospitality Services JSC (KBC's local vehicle) via DT Marks Vietnam LLC (79% DTTM Operations, 20% Trump family); Vietnamese reports suggest part of it was still a receivable. India: the same 2025 report (covering 2024) shows at least $12M from India, of which $10M was a 'development fee' from Reliance 4IR Realty Development (a Reliance Industries unit) for a Mumbai project that has not been identified (see C70), and about $2.2M in licence and royalty fees from Tribeca, M3M units, Lodha, Unimark and RDB. These fees were paid before or around the start of the term, not as tariff-era payments. Per-project 2025 figures for India, Indonesia, Georgia, Romania and the Maldives were not found; aggregates remain CREW's >$117M foreign revenue in 2025 and the FT's $63M in licensing/management.

sub_claims.statement: The second-term ethics pledge permits these deals, and its limits.
sub_claims.finding: As established in C31, the 10 Jan 2025 Trump Organization ethics policy dropped the first-term ban on new foreign deals. It bars deals directly with foreign governments but allows deals with private foreign companies, adds an outside ethics adviser, and keeps Trump out of day-to-day management. Every project here has a private developer as counterparty (KBC, MNC, Tribeca, SDC, Dar Global, Georgian developers), so all are permitted on paper. The pledge's limits are that it does not cover deals whose approvals, land or permits come from foreign governments: Vietnam's deputy-PM approval and state land clearance, Serbia's special law, and Georgia's land bought from a fund linked to the sanctioned ruling-party founder. It also does not stop family members meeting heads of government. The Trump Organization says it is 'fully compliant with all applicable ethics and conflicts of interest laws'.

corrections: Brief implies the Hung Yen deal arose during tariff talks; it was signed in October 2024, before the election and the April 2025 tariffs. What came during the talks was the fast-tracked approval (May 2025) and groundbreaking (21 May 2025).
Brief says the Ho Chi Minh City tower advanced; as of Nov 2026 it remains a proposal with in-principle backing, with no confirmed approval or construction.

Brief says Indonesian MNC/Hary Tanoe resorts 'advanced'; they date from 2015-2019 and were halted by Indonesia's Environment Ministry in February 2025. A lift of the suspension is reported only by one trade outlet (Aug 2026).

Brief lumps India in as a country granted favours; US tariffs on India rose to 50% in Aug 2025 while Trump-branded launches continued, and the Feb 2026 cut to 18% was tied to Russian oil, not property.
CREW's count has been 21, 24 and 25 at different times; '~24' is a fair snapshot.

The fees line is not wholly undisclosed: Trump's 2025 disclosure shows a $5M Vietnam licence fee (Hung Yen Hospitality via DT Marks Vietnam) and at least $12M from India for 2024, $10M of it from a Reliance unit.
denials_and_context: The White House told the NYT that 'all of the president's trade discussions are totally unrelated to the Trump Organization', and has said neither the president nor his family has ever engaged in conflicts of interest.
The Trump Organization says it is fully compliant with ethics and conflict laws, that it only licenses its brand, and that in Vietnam it is not involved in investment or farmer compensation.
Eric Trump said he had not met Prabowo after the hot-mic exchange.
Ivanishvili's lawyer says the family donated most of the former racecourse land to the state for a public park.

Context: the 2025 ethics policy, unlike 2017's, allows private foreign deals and bars only deals directly with foreign governments. Counterparties here are private, but approvals, land and laws come from governments, which the policy does not address.
Vietnam's tariff relief (46% to 20%) is similar to outcomes for neighbours without Trump projects; a counterfactual comparison was not done here, so causation is not established.

Research limits: CREW, Asia Sentinel, WSJ and NYT pages could not be fetched; several findings rest on syndications and search summaries. The search budget ran out before India fee figures and the AP April 2026 piece could be checked in detail.
